subject: Escalation: approval for automated revert + account-targeted pin during phased rollout
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: enable automated revert + account-targeted pin for Acme during phased rollout

Team —

TL;DR: Acme (ACME-2026-EXP01) is seeing intermittent P99 latency regressions on the new quantized v5.2 variant during our phased rollout. I’m requesting authorization to enable (a) an automated revert trigger for their traffic slice and (b) a short-term account-targeted version pin (soft pin) as a mitigation while we investigate root cause. This would be active only for Acme’s requests and should not affect global routing.

Why: Over the last 8 hours the canary bucket (5% traffic) for v5.2 shows a reproducible P99 latency jump from ~85ms to 340–410ms after KV-cache pressure increases during long context sessions. We have a mitigation plan that avoids a full platform rollback and keeps the SLA-bound customer online.

Proposal (concise):
- Canary slice: keep at 5% for next 48h.
- Auto-revert trigger: if Acme-specific P99 > 300ms for two consecutive 10-minute windows OR error-rate increase > 0.8% over baseline, automatically route their traffic back to v5.1 for up to 72h.
- Account-targeted soft pin: once revert happens, pin Acme’s requests to v5.1 for 72 hours (pin recorded in routing metadata and overrideable by ops).
- Observability: push alert to #sre-acme and exec summary to Monica/Laura. Attachments: canary-metrics-20270418.png + pin-playbook-20270418.pdf

Risks:
- Slight complexity in routing tables; we'll use existing per-account routing keys and feature flags.
- Potential long-tail divergence if multiple accounts need pins simultaneously; we will cap concurrent targeted pins to 8 accounts per region.

Ask: please approve the above emergency fallback and pin for Acme. If approved, SRE will coordinate the activation window and I’ll notify Acme’s SRE and account team.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priyom —

Thanks for the quick write-up. A few clarifying questions before I sign off:
1) Can you confirm the exact routing key you'd use to scope to Acme (team wants deterministic selector).
2) Is the 300ms P99 threshold calibrated to their SLA (we need to avoid flipping for normal variance).
3) Who's the ops owner that can manually undo the pin if we see false positives?
4) Does this plan require changes to customer-facing SLA language or credits if the auto-revert engages?

If you can answer inline — I’ll prioritise review.

–Monica

Subject: Re: Request: enable automated revert + account-targeted pin for Acme during phased rollout

Monica —

Answers inline:
1) Routing key: account_id = ACME-12345 (this maps to the per-tenant routing shard we already use for dedicated routing). We'll add a selector flag: routing.meta.customer_tag == "acme:prod" so it’s explicit.
2) Threshold: 300ms P99 is conservative relative to Acme’s SLA (they have 250ms p99 target). We chose 300ms to avoid flip for small jitter; the two consecutive 10-minute window condition reduces flapping.
3) Ops owners: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) is the manual override. He can clear pins using the routing-control console. We’ll also include a failsafe: a human-in-the-loop hold that requires explicit approval to unpin within first 2 hours after an automated pin.
4) SLA/credits: This is a mitigation to keep them online; legal suggested we document the incident and we will not auto-issue credits unless we later determine a platform fault that caused the regression. If Acme requests credits up-front, we’ll escalate to Revenue Ops.

I also want to highlight: the playbook includes a limited concurrent-pin cap and a rollback-to-stable timeline to avoid prolonged divergence. See pin-playbook-20270418.pdf for the exact console steps.

If that looks good I’d request approval for immediate activation window (start: 2027-04-18T11:00 PDT) for 48h monitoring.

Priyom

Team / Acme —

Post-activation summary: during the 48h monitoring window we observed one automatic revert event at 2027-04-19T02:14 PDT for Acme (account_id ACME-12345). 
- Trigger: Acme-specific P99 exceeded 300ms for two consecutive 10-minute windows.
- Action taken: routing automatically shifted their traffic to v5.1 and a soft pin (72h) was applied.
- Impact: no user-visible errors; median latency improved to 95ms post-revert.
- Next steps: root-cause triage with runtime team scheduled for 2027-04-21.

Laura — per your condition: this is a single revert within 24h so no credit escalation. We’ll include the incident write-up and metrics in the Confluence page linked below.
